*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: {{workspace:task/olivia-grant/spec-scheduler-v2}}/artifacts/experiments/context-aware-speculation.md
+# Context-aware speculative scheduling prototype
+
+## Evidence
+
+- RFC #48627 says profitable speculative depth depends on both scheduled batch
+  size and decode-time context length. It requires compatibility with existing
+  three-field entries, a five-field batch/context form, rectangular coverage,
+  and staged scheduler integration
+  (`/code/upstream-issues/vllm-48627.md`,
+  `enterprise_a251a0a0364578007031aba8`).
+- Redwood's speculative runtime acceptance matrix targets at least 20% p95
+  token-latency improvement on long-context workloads, no more than 8% token
+  cost increase, and no more than 1% eval-score loss. It calls for deterministic
+  replay, a 48-hour soak, staged canaries, and rollback on sustained latency,
+  error, quality, waste/cost, or OOM regressions
+  (`/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/speculative-runtime-acceptance-rollback-matrix.json`,
+  `dsid_b218fd2b04a041df876e8d57571ecc98`).
+- Redwood's representative workload gate requires generated prompt-length
+  p50/p90/p95 to match production telemetry within 10%, output-length
+  p50/p90/p95 within 15%, and concurrency to reproduce production burstiness
+  (`/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4823-representative-chat-streaming-workload.json`,
+  `dsid_bf69afe8fe964eb8af7032530bac7c72`).
+- The LTS baseline deliberately disables speculative decoding because its
+  performance is sensitive to model and request-distribution changes. Default
+  gates fail generative-throughput regressions beyond 2% on H100/H200 and TTFT
+  p95 regressions beyond 3%; this prototype therefore does not claim a
+  performance win
+  (`/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/lts-perf-baseline-results-2025q3-sheet.json`,
+  `dsid_cd22e1d3a7324c4fb8987cb2afdc947f`).
+- Current vLLM dynamic speculation is incompatible with data parallelism
+  because ranks may choose different K values and deadlock. Full CUDA graphs
+  require model runner v2; these constraints remain unchanged
+  (`/code/vllm/docs/features/speculative_decoding/dynamic_speculative_decoding.md`,
+  `enterprise_388e5a3454904e151772c045`).
+
+## Staged design
+
+Schema stage:
+
+- Preserve legacy `(batch_start, batch_end, K)` entries and their carry-forward
+  gap behavior.
+- Add `(batch_start, batch_end, context_start, context_end, K)` entries.
+- Require one entry arity per schedule, positive inclusive ranges, nonnegative
+  K, and an exact non-overlapping tiling from `(1, 1)` through the configured
+  maxima.
+- Expand the five-field form into a dense, one-indexed
+  `batch_size -> context_length -> K` table and clamp K to the runtime maximum.
+
+Scheduler stage:
+
+- Build the dense table once using `max_num_seqs` and `max_model_len`.
+- At the existing final K-selection boundary, use scheduled-request count and
+  the maximum `num_computed_tokens` among requests scheduled in that step.
+  Maximum context is a conservative representative for KV-read cost and uses
+  state already held by the scheduler.
+- Keep the legacy one-dimensional lookup path intact. CUDA graph query lengths
+  continue to be derived from the configured K values; only tuple indexing is
+  generalized from position 2 to the final field. No graph shape policy,
+  capture set, KV buffer, or GPU allocation behavior is changed.
+
+## Checks performed
+
+- `uv run --no-project python -m compileall` on all changed Python files:
+  passed.
+- `uvx ruff check` on all changed Python files: passed.
+- Direct CPU execution of the schema helper covered legacy compatibility,
+  valid rectangular lookup, gaps, and overlaps: passed.
+- Focused pytest invocation was attempted through `uv`, but the mounted
+  environment has no pytest installation (`No module named pytest`).
+
+## Assumptions and GPU experiments still required
+
+The following remain unvalidated performance assumptions:
+
+- Maximum scheduled context is a better representative than mean, median, or
+  token-weighted context for selecting a single batch-wide K.
+- A dense table sized by `max_num_seqs * max_model_len` is acceptable for
+  deployed maximum context configurations.
+- Context-aware K selection improves the long-context slices without reducing
+  short-context throughput or increasing speculative waste beyond gates.
+
+Required GPU work:
+
+1. Sweep batch, context, K, model/drafter, quantization, and GPU SKU with warm
+   and cold KV-cache mixes. Include 1k, 2k, 8k, 16k, and 32k context buckets.
+2. Compare maximum, median, and token-weighted representative context against a
+   per-request oracle.
+3. Verify CUDA graph capture/replay for every selected K on model runner v1
+   piecewise mode and model runner v2 full graphs.
+4. Replay a production-matched context and concurrency distribution; measure
+   p50/p95 token latency, throughput, acceptance length, waste ratio, cost,
+   memory pressure, and quality.
+5. Run deterministic output comparison, 48-hour soak, and staged canary gates.
+   Keep data-parallel fallback enabled until rank-consistent K selection has a
+   separate design and deadlock validation.
*** End Patch
